TEXT: A Xience Alpine stent was significantly shorter after deployment; no adverse patient effects or clinically significant delay were reported.
After post-dilatation, no flow was seen in the distal scaffold; the physician suspected dissection or an embolized clot.
The patient presented with pain in the lower left leg and angiogram revealed scaffold thrombosis; no treatment was given.
During surgery, imaging acquisition was difficult; handswitch operation failed and the team switched to a footswitch, resolving the issue.
The valve leaflet could not open and the product was replaced; no patient complications were reported.
The system had pump hardware and communication errors; attempts to resolve them failed and the procedure was aborted.
Resistance was encountered while advancing the stent; it could not be retrieved and was deployed distal to the aneurysm.
A screw disengaged during surgery, requiring replacement; the procedure had a 90-minute delay and hospitalization was extended three days.
Resistance persisted during stent advancement, causing premature deployment; the device was replaced and no patient discomfort was reported.
After ablation, the patient developed asystole and hypotension; chest compressions were performed and the patient was transferred to intensive care.
The distal balloon and catheter tip detached, causing vessel occlusion; the procedure was stopped because of patient instability.
The patient experienced an acute ischemic stroke after pulsed-field ablation, with slurred speech and facial asymmetry.
The monitor was left in demo mode overnight, and the displayed cardiac output may have been used as a reference.
Air entered the patient during the procedure; no symptoms occurred and the patient remained stable.
Attempts to pass the valve through the access site were unsuccessful; a small vessel tear occurred and was repaired.
The harmonic ace tip broke during surgery; it was replaced and no patient consequence was reported.
The system developed non-recoverable faults and communication errors; service engineers replaced setup joints and verified the system.
The instrument had a damaged grip cable; the event was confirmed by failure analysis.
The device alarmed for air in the line; the patient felt wetness and therapy was ended with no injury reported.
The infusion device under-infused, and the patient was readmitted to the hospital after the expected infusion time.
The infusion device under-infused because the patient did not maintain the device at the same height as the line insertion.
The patient underwent revision surgery five months after implantation due to anterior dislocation; soft-tissue and cup positioning were factors.
A patient reported anterior knee pain after surgery; the report did not provide a treatment timeframe.
The patient required revision surgery because a hip liner was compromised, resulting in pain.
Medication leaked between the syringe and needle hub; the connection required force and twisting, raising questions about the instructions.
The safety mechanism failed during use, causing the needle core to retract and become unusable.
The peripheral IV catheter was associated with a material puncture or hole and vascular perforation.
The suture broke after the first stitch; staff replaced it and no adverse effects on wound healing were reported.
A suture malfunction was reported; the device was not returned and additional information was requested.
A surgical mesh report involved erosion, pain, and discomfort; additional patient and procedure information was requested.
